minor_characters.name: Adolph
minor_characters.appearances_summary: St. Clare’s stylish valet in New Orleans; appears in household comedy, banter with other servants, and at the auction; has no bearing on Tom’s moral arc or fate.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His scenes are comic color that don’t affect the escape plot, Eva’s sanctifying influence, St. Clare’s conversion arc, or Tom’s ultimate martyrdom.

minor_characters.name: Rosa (and Jane)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: St. Clare household chambermaids who snipe at Topsy and figure in a side episode where Marie orders Rosa whipped.
minor_characters.reason_removable: They function as foils in house scenes but removing them does not change any principal character’s development or the plot’s direction.

minor_characters.name: Dinah
minor_characters.appearances_summary: St. Clare’s formidable cook whose clashes with Miss Ophelia over kitchens and ‘clarin’ up’ supply domestic comedy.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her kitchen-war episodes are comic set‑pieces that can be summarized in a line about Ophelia’s culture clash without changing plot or theme.

minor_characters.name: Mammy (Marie's nurse)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Marie's long‑suffering personal attendant who frets over Eva and tends Marie’s ‘nervous’ spells.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her presence underscores Marie’s selfishness but is not needed once Marie’s character is shown and Eva’s sanctity is established.

minor_characters.name: Alfred St. Clare
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Augustine’s aristocratic brother; debates politics and hierarchy during a brief lake visit.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His ideological sparring adds redundancy to themes already expressed by Augustine and Marie and does not affect Tom’s sale or St. Clare’s turn.

minor_characters.name: Henrique St. Clare
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Alfred’s son who abuses his groom Dodo during the lake visit to illustrate learned cruelty.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The episode is illustrative but not structurally necessary; St. Clare’s household already shows the contradictions of slavery.

minor_characters.name: Dodo
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Henrique’s young groom mistreated during the lake chapters.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is only a foil for Henrique’s cruelty; cutting him with that visit removes no plot driver.

minor_characters.name: Prue
minor_characters.appearances_summary: An enslaved woman in New Orleans whose abuse and death are reported in a side episode.
minor_characters.reason_removable: She is a powerful vignette but not required to follow Eva’s arc, St. Clare’s death, or Tom’s journey to Legree.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Marks
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Tom Loker’s slippery associate in the slave‑catching scenes around the tavern and the river chase.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Eliza’s flight and Loker’s wounding can be retained without this extra pursuer; he neither reforms nor returns to influence outcomes.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Skeggs (dealer) and ‘B. & Co.’ New York partners
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Warehouse keeper and the northern firm that consigns Susan and Emmeline to sale before Legree buys them.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Emmeline can be introduced upon Legree’s plantation without this detailed provenance; the theme of northern complicity survives elsewhere.

minor_characters.name: Susan (Emmeline’s mother)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Respectable mulatto mother separated from Emmeline at the New Orleans auction, then disappears.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her tragic split amplifies the theme but Emmeline’s role with Cassy and Legree is intact without her mother’s scenes.

minor_characters.name: Aunt Dorcas
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A Quaker woman who nurses the wounded slave-catcher Tom Loker in Ch 038 and presides, with comic firmness, over his convalescence.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her scenes only soften Loker and duplicate the novel’s broader Quaker-kindness thread, which the synopsis already preserves without needing her as a distinct figure.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Smyth
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A respectable woman in Ch 038 who poses as Harry’s 'aunty' to help the party embark at Sandusky.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her helpful role can be absorbed by unnamed Quaker or free Black allies without altering the escape.

minor_characters.name: Tiger and Fury (Legree’s dogs)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Named man-hunting dogs uncoupled for the swamp hunt in Ch 040.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The generic threat of tracking dogs suffices and the plot does not hinge on their names or personalities.

minor_characters.name: Tompkins
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A neighboring planter Legree mentions in Ch 036 when boasting about crop wagers.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He exists only to illustrate Legree’s vanity and can be excised without affecting events or themes.

minor_characters.name: Captain Stuart
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The gentleman who later buys and kindly keeps Cassy in Ch 035 before dying of cholera.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His named identity is incidental to Cassy’s trauma; her essential backstory (seduced, sold, children torn away) reads the same if his name never appears.

minor_characters.name: Butler
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The principal white exploiter in Cassy’s backstory in Ch 035, who sells her children and abuses her.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is a backstory placeholder for 'the master who abused me' and need not be named for her arc or the themes to land.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Simmons
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A prior seller named in Ch 043 when George mentions Eliza’s bill of sale, which triggers Cassy’s faint.
minor_characters.reason_removable: The specific seller’s name is irrelevant; the recognition moment works without it.

minor_characters.name: Sally
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A Shelby house servant invoked in Ch 045 during Aunt Chloe’s comic fussing over the teapot.
minor_characters.reason_removable: She is a one-line domestic mention whose absence does not affect the freeing scene or themes.

minor_characters.name: Polly
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Aunt Chloe’s little daughter mentioned in Ch 045 during the kitchen prelude to George Shelby’s return.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Naming the child adds homely color only; the manumission scene and its meaning are unchanged if she is unnamed or omitted.

subplots.name: Aunt Chloe hired out as a Louisville confectioner to buy Tom’s freedom
subplots.reason_removable: It is a touching sidetrack that never alters Tom’s sale to Legree or his martyrdom; Shelby’s later manumission scene stands without it.

subplots.name: Miss Ophelia’s housekeeping crusade against Dinah (kitchen wars, closets, Yankee methods)
subplots.reason_removable: These culture‑clash episodes can be compressed to a line about Ophelia’s reforming zeal without affecting Ophelia, Topsy, or Eva’s arcs.

subplots.name: Henrique & Dodo at the lake (visit from Alfred St. Clare)
subplots.reason_removable: The visit’s cruelty vignette and class talk duplicate themes already shown by Marie and Augustine and do not change any later choice or event.

subplots.name: Rosa’s whipping order and household disciplinary subplot
subplots.reason_removable: It further blackens Marie but adds no new consequence to the main plot; Marie’s character is clear without it.

subplots.name: Back‑gammon politics & theology (Alfred vs. Augustine; long salon debates)
subplots.reason_removable: St. Clare’s moral movement and conversion can be conveyed in fewer, tighter scenes; extended set‑piece debates slow the story.

subplots.name: New York ‘Christian’ firm B. & Co. consigning Susan & Emmeline
subplots.reason_removable: Northern complicity is already indicted elsewhere; Emmeline can simply be part of Legree’s purchase without the firm’s backstory.

subplots.name: Sam & Andy’s comic delaying of Haley with the horses
subplots.reason_removable: It’s beloved comic relief, but Eliza’s crossing and the Quaker rescue remain clear and urgent without this detour.

subplots.name: Topsy’s extended catechism-and-stealing lessons before Eva befriends her
subplots.reason_removable: Keep Topsy’s introduction and her change under Eva; the earlier, lengthy discipline episodes can be summarized.

subplots.name: Tom Loker’s convalescence and softening under a Quaker nurse
subplots.reason_removable: His comedy-of-recovery and partial reform neither affect George and Eliza’s successful crossing nor any endpoint in the synopsis.

subplots.name: Marks’s last-minute bluff on the Sandusky steamer
subplots.reason_removable: The escape by lake can proceed without this extra near-catch, which only adds suspense beats.

subplots.name: Emmeline’s marriage to the ship’s first mate
subplots.reason_removable: This epilogue-style coda does not figure in the synopsis and can be dropped without affecting Cassy and Emmeline’s escape or later reunions.

subplots.name: Postscript discovery of Cassy’s son
subplots.reason_removable: A feel-good addendum not required by the synopsis’s closures (Cassy’s reunion with Eliza and George Harris’s Liberia decision).

subplots.name: Shelby kitchen prelude (Aunt Chloe’s wage bills, teapot talk) before George’s return
subplots.reason_removable: It’s charming domestic business that can be pruned to get to the manumission scene without loss of plot or theme.

subplots.name: Why George Shelby arrives too late (lost letter, estate business)
subplots.reason_removable: Abridgments can state simply that he came 'too late' per the synopsis without explaining postal mishaps and probate errands.

digressions.topic: Long comic tableau of a Kentucky tavern culture (hats, lounging, types) before Mr. Wilson meets George
digressions.reason_removable: A colorful regional sketch that delays George’s reveal without adding plot or character insight unavailable elsewhere.

digressions.topic: Extended scenic-prose on the Mississippi and the steamer as emblem
digressions.reason_removable: Beautiful set dressing that can be condensed to a line without reducing the New Orleans transition or Tom–Eva meeting.

digressions.topic: Augustine St. Clare’s multi‑page backstory and social philosophy
digressions.reason_removable: Abridgers can précis his upbringing and disillusion in a paragraph; the full essayistic excursus stalls momentum.

digressions.topic: Minute household treatise on Miss Ophelia’s northern methods (drawers, napkins, nutmegs)
digressions.reason_removable: Comic domestic taxonomy that doesn’t advance plot or inner change; a sentence can establish Ophelia’s exacting nature.

digressions.topic: Authorial essay on slaves’ distress when kind masters die
digressions.reason_removable: A powerful aside that repeats sentiments already shown in scene through Tom and the household; can be folded into narrative.

digressions.topic: Direct addresses to ‘refined readers’ and a homily on the genteel packaging of slave warehouses
digressions.reason_removable: The sermonizing frame can be trimmed while keeping the auction action that moves Tom and Emmeline to Legree.

digressions.topic: Extended travelogue and ruin-porn descriptions of the swamp road, decayed grounds, and house exteriors on arrival at Legree’s.
digressions.reason_removable: Mood-setting paragraphs can be compressed to a line without changing the events that follow.

digressions.topic: Rhetorical apostrophe to 'Liberty' and civic sermonizing during the lake crossing.
digressions.reason_removable: The escape and landing in Canada read cleanly without the essayistic aside.

digressions.topic: Full hymn lyrics and a general treatise on slave religious experience framing Tom’s vision.
digressions.reason_removable: Tom’s crisis and consolation can be summarized with one or two lyric snippets instead of pages of quotation and commentary.

digressions.topic: Philosophical asides on superstition and the 'godless man' amid the garret-haunting setup.
digressions.reason_removable: They are thematic glosses that can be trimmed while keeping the garret stratagem clear.

digressions.topic: Opening ghost-lore excursus (Hamlet nod, 'sheeted dead,' media satire) before returning to Cassy’s ruse.
digressions.reason_removable: Comedic theorizing about ghosts isn’t needed to follow the escape plot.

digressions.topic: Long poetic epigraph and ornamental verse prelude ('Bryant') to Tom’s martyrdom chapter.
digressions.reason_removable: Chapter epigraphs are decorative and can be dropped in an abridgment without narrative loss.

digressions.topic: Second-person moral apostrophes and theological riffing ('Ye who have wondered…') around Legree’s hair-token panic.
digressions.reason_removable: The mother’s lock of hair and its effect on Legree remain clear without the surrounding homiletics.
